name: StrongMinds (SoGive, March 2024)
summary: Group interpersonal therapy for depression in Uganda and Zambia, delivered by StrongMinds' staff, volunteers and partner organisations. A re-implementation of SoGive's cost-effectiveness analysis, which counts depression averted in SoGive's DALYs: lowering depression by about 23 PHQ-9 points for a year counts as one year of healthy life. This is the version SoGive published in March 2024 (StrongMinds 6 of 9), at StrongMinds' 2023 cost per person.

sections.title: Effect of therapy on the client
Discounting
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not SoGive's. SoGive counts the months of better mood after therapy the same whenever they come. In our view, later months count a little less at the discount rate under Your values, as in GiveWell's models; the evaluator view sets the rate to 0, so SoGive's numbers reproduce.

rows.label: Effect of therapy on depression, average trial patient
rows.explainer: SoGive's pooled effect size, in standard deviations of depression scores, from the METAPSY database of psychotherapy trials: studies passing four risk-of-bias criteria, outliers removed, then trim-and-fill correction for publication bias. See SoGive's "What's the effect size of therapy?" (StrongMinds 3 of 9).

rows.label: Adjustment for 6 sessions (trials average 9)
rows.explainer: From SoGive's meta-regression of effect size on the number of sessions: StrongMinds' groups run about 6 sessions, fewer than the average trial.

rows.label: Duration of the benefit for patients who fully recover
rows.explainer: SoGive combines spontaneous remission rates with relapse rates for treated patients who recovered (StrongMinds 4 of 9: the benefit is shorter-lived than earlier estimates). In years of full effect after treatment ends.

rows.label: Adjustment for the average treated patient
rows.explainer: SoGive's judgment: the duration above comes from patients who reached remission, which may be optimistic for the average patient, so SoGive takes 90% of it.

rows.label: Length of a 6-session course
rows.explainer: Six weekly sessions. Some of the improvement happens during the course, counted as half the effect over its length.

rows.label: Depression averted per client treated
rows.formula: effect_size_sds * sessions_adjustment * duration_years_recovered * duration_adjustment_average * discount_factor + intervention_length_years * sessions_adjustment * effect_size_sds / 2
rows.explainer: The area under the curve of improvement over time: the full effect for the adjusted duration after the course, plus half the effect during the course. In our view the part after the course is discounted (see Discounting); SoGive doesn't discount, and the evaluator view sets the rate to 0.

rows.label: Discount rate on future benefits
rows.explainer: The shared discount rate (Your values). SoGive doesn't discount, so the evaluator view pins it at 0.

rows.label: Same rate, compounded continuously
Years of full benefit after the course
Discount factor for the benefit after the course
rows.explainer: The average discount over the months the full effect lasts, starting when the course ends. Small: the benefit lasts well under a year.

rows.explainer: Taken by SoGive from GiveWell's assessment of HLI's StrongMinds analysis.

Depression averted per person treated, including household
Spread (SD) of depression scores before treatment
rows.explainer: Standard deviation of PHQ-9 scores of trial participants before treatment, from the METAPSY database. The effect size above is in these standard deviations.

rows.label: Depression score at which most people would rather experience nothing
rows.explainer: SoGive's moral weight for depression (StrongMinds 5 of 9): from time-trade-off and rating-scale data, a PHQ-9 score of about 23 is as bad as not existing, so lowering depression by 23 points for a year counts as one year of healthy life (SoGive's "DALY of depression").

rows.label: Depression averted that counts as one year of healthy life
rows.explainer: 23 PHQ-9 points in standard deviations: about 5.5 SD-years of depression averted are worth one DALY on SoGive's scale.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: DALYs averted per dollar
rows.explainer: SoGive's cost per DALY turned into DALYs per dollar; with credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest). SoGive's DALYs of depression count one for one as years of healthy life (the standard path for DALYs). They are SoGive's own measure, not counted burden-of-disease DALYs: SoGive counts a year 23 PHQ-9 points less depressed as one, from time-trade-off data, where the Global Burden of Disease weight for severe depression (0.658) would count it as about two thirds of one. SoGive's own benchmarks also value one such year at four doublings of income, twice our default exchange rate, so SoGive's verdict (about twice as good as cash) reads lower here.
